thread:
Alice Chang: handing off to Tom now — ongoing customer-facing latency spike on text-gen endpoints, started ~02:12 UTC. I’m primary until 02:30 then Tom, you’re primary; Priya you’re secondary. summary: increased p95 from 180ms -> 1.2s, errors small but retries visible. running mitigations: fallback to smaller model (gpt-small-compat) for low-priority routes, autoscaler bumped pool-2 by +2 nodes. Incident link: https://pager.redwood/INC-4321 :eyes:
incident-bot: [02:18 UTC] ALERT: high_latency detected on /v1/generate cluster=us-west-2 group=text-gen p95=1.2s threshold=300ms
Tom O'Neill: ack — taking primary at 02:30. quick question: do we have any live customer tickets? Jenna, you were triaging?
Jenna Rivera: we got two support tickets, both low-volume customers complaining about slow responses. I replied with status and ETA ~30m.
Priya Patel: noted. I'll watch logs and tracing during handoff. Runbook reference: https://confluence.redwood/runbooks/text-gen-latency — started the "reduce-batch-size" path, also caching lookups enabled for common prefixes.
Marco Li: FYI I pushed a temporary config to routing policy to route 10% of free-tier requests to dedicated-fallback to keep paid latency good.
Alice Chang: handoff checklist: 1) confirm primary/secondary 2) confirm mitigations ran 3) post impact estimate 4) open follow-up tickets 5) schedule retro. I've already done 1-2.
Tom O'Neill: got it. during handoff I'll watch metrics dashboard and traces. If error rate >0.5% or p95 >1.5s we escalate to SRE pager. Any outstanding gaps?
Priya Patel: coverage gap — no one on night shift owns the dedicated-fallback autoscaler policy; if it flaps we might not notice. Suggest action item to add alert for autoscaler scale-down failures.
Alice Chang: good catch. please file ticket for alert.
Priya Patel: filing now — TICKET-789: add alert for autoscaler scale-down failures and owner tag.
ops-bot: [02:40 UTC] TICKET-789 created by Priya Patel -> https://issues.redwood/TICKET-789
Tom O'Neill: quick operational note — probed a few pods, some had 100% cpu on attention kernel during long sequences. ran this command to check: ```kubectl top pods -n text-gen | grep model-```
Tom O'Neill: results: model-serve-12 2000m CPU, model-serve-9 1900m CPU; I've rotated a few requests off those pods.
Jenna Rivera: support updated customers: "we've applied temporary routing and smaller models to reduce latency, monitoring for improvement; we'll update after handoff." :white_check_mark:
Alice Chang: handing over logs and traces: Sentry link https://sentry.redwood/issue/9887 and trace sample https://traces.redwood/trace/abcd1234
Tom O'Neill: taking over now. I'll keep primary until 05:00 UTC. Priya you remain secondary. Jenna continue support comms. Marco — if routing changes are needed please stand by.
Marco Li: on it. If p95 doesn't drop below 400ms in 20m, I'll promote another node pool and widen fallback to 25%.
Tom O'Neill: update 02:58 UTC — p95 down to 540ms after fallback, errors steady at 0.12%. Good progress but still above SLO.
Priya Patel: checking traces, root cause partially KV cache churn on long contexts. Runbook suggests increasing prefix cache TTL for heavy routes, but that could increase cost. Opening follow-up ticket: TICKET-790: investigate KV cache churn + tuning.
ops-bot: [03:05 UTC] TICKET-790 created by Priya Patel -> https://issues.redwood/TICKET-790
Alice Chang: action items to carry forward (post-handoff): - TICKET-789 (autoscaler alert) assignee Priya - TICKET-790 (KV cache investigation) assignee Marco - Post-incident retro scheduled, tentative Wed 14:00 UTC (calendar invite to follow) - Customer impact summary for execs (Jenna to draft)
Jenna Rivera: I'll draft the customer impact summary and post to #customer-success, will include affected request volumes and mitigation timeline.
Tom O'Neill: 03:45 UTC — p95 stabilized ~320ms, errors 0.08%. I'll keep watching but feel comfortable handing back to day shift.
Alice Chang: thanks Tom. final handoff notes: please include any config changes in the changelog and link PRs. Who will own the retro?
Marco Li: I can run the retro, include infra, runtime, devex. will prepare a short blameless timeline and 3 action items.
Priya Patel: tagging owners in tickets now.
incident-bot: [04:10 UTC] INCIDENT INC-4321 status => mitigated (partial) note="fallback routing + smaller model reduced latency; investigation tickets opened"
Tom O'Neill: last item — follow-up: add a synthetic test for long-context KV churn scenarios. Adding to backlog as TICKET-791.
ops-bot: [04:22 UTC] TICKET-791 created by Tom O'Neill -> https://issues.redwood/TICKET-791
Alice Chang: thanks team. I'll update the incident doc with timeline and link tickets. Final handoff complete at 04:30 UTC. :rocket:
